hook: A palladium catalyst attaches aryl groups to plain arenes at the most open C-H site.
hook_turn: at the most open C-H site.
summary: A palladium catalyst system joins aryl groups directly to C-H bonds in simple arenes, favoring the sterically most exposed site. It pairs a tailored catalyst environment with an advanced precatalyst and diaryliodonium reagents. Even benzene can be arylated repeatedly, and mild conditions allow late-stage use and groups that normal cross-coupling would destroy. Scope is shown on selected substrates, so performance on other molecules is untested.
title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C-H arylation of arenes.
